A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSDrive research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references. All 12 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v2 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original FSDrive trajectory-planning, image-generation, and scene-understanding results, together with ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds FSDrive evaluation on NAVSIM in Table 2.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the vocabulary expansion, progressive image generation, unified visual CoT, trajectory prediction, and two-stage training procedure. Replacing VLM with VLA terminology does not establish an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: v2 adds NAVSIM evaluation covering challenging changes in driving intent while excluding static and constant-speed situations, extending the represented driving scenarios beyond the retained nuScenes and DriveLM evaluations.

E2.justification: The new NAVSIM comparison includes VADv2, DiffusionDrive-Cam, LTF, PARA-Drive, and LAW, alongside UniAD. Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged; OminiDrive is corrected to OmniDrive rather than replaced.

E3.justification: v2 introduces camera-only NAVSIM navtest evaluation in a pseudo closed-loop setting, reporting NC, DAC, TTC, Comf., EP, and PDMS. This adds a distinct evaluation protocol; the previously reported splits, training budgets, and nuScenes/DriveLM metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The pretraining-component, CoT-type, data-volume, and progressive-generation ablations are retained unchanged, as is Figure 3's incorrect-navigation-instruction case study. NAVSIM adds benchmark evaluation rather than a new diagnostic or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. The added NAVSIM results use the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds the NAVSIM results in Table 2, including FSDrive PDMS 85.1 versus LAW 84.6 and DiffusionDrive-Cam 83.6. Numerical results in all six original tables are retained in v2 Tables 1 and 3–7; the addition is new benchmark evidence, not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(6) remain unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, derivations, or formal properties are added; the new NAVSIM metrics are listed without mathematical definitions.

C1.justification: The rewritten abstract extends the stated performance claims to NAVSIM, while the three methodological contributions and conclusion remain substantively unchanged. It groups nuScenes and NAVSIM under ST-P3/UniAD metrics, although Table 2 reports PDMS and its components for NAVSIM.

C2.justification: The physical-constraint, inverse-dynamics, and modality-gap explanations and the front-view-only limitation remain unchanged. The added future-work sentence about larger datasets and a better unified paradigm repeats the existing scaling direction and adds no substantive failure condition or mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: v2's abstract newly states that code is available and supplies a repository address. The existing hardware, epochs, learning rate, batch size, and MoVQGAN implementation details are unchanged; repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The bibliography substantially changes, adding NAVSIM and new planning comparators while removing works including Chameleon, MetaMorph, LMDrive, and STaR. Attribution also changes materially: Section 2.1 replaces Chameleon and SEED in the 0.3% training-cost comparison with references including GDiffRetro, DAMMFND, and SecTOW, without explaining their relevance.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, changes VLM/VLA terminology, corrects OmniDrive spelling, updates affiliation numbering and the conference footer, and adds acknowledgments. Most body prose and the section hierarchy remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the NAVSIM table, reformats the generation and DriveLM tables, and relocates/resizes Figure 3. The original figures and table contents remain present, with subsequent tables renumbered and surrounding pages reflowed.

improvement.justification: NAVSIM evaluation and the code-access pointer improve empirical coverage and reproducibility information. However, the unexplained citation substitutions supporting the training-cost comparison weaken attribution, and the abstract groups NAVSIM with ST-P3/UniAD metrics despite Table 2 using PDMS and its components. These benefits and reporting problems leave the net quality direction uncertain from the supplied PDFs.
